target_customer: Corporations buying forest carbon credits, plus project developers needing verification
problem: Buyers distrusted forest carbon offsets because quality was hard to verify. Pachama used satellite imagery and machine learning to monitor forest carbon and sell vetted credits.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on carbon credits plus MRV software
product_category: Forest carbon credit marketplace and monitoring

founders.name: Diego Saez Gil
founders.background_notes: YC page: serial entrepreneur and environmentalist from northern Argentina.

founders.name: Tomas Aftalion
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Estimating forest carbon stocks from satellite, LiDAR and drone data with machine learning requires remote sensing expertise and ground-truth data, which is difficult for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Data and models on forest carbon improve with projects onboarded, but verification methods were copyable by funded rivals and credit supply was controlled by project developers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Registries and consultants did not copy the model quickly; later rivals such as Sylvera emerged, and a consulting-led firm, Carbon Direct, bought Pachama in 2025.

market_need_then: Corporate net-zero pledges were growing and offset quality was questioned; Microsoft was reported using Pachama for forest carbon tracking in early 2020.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven; restoring nature to solve climate change

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity angels reported by TechCrunch (Ellen DeGeneres, Laura Dern, Serena Williams) added press attention.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognised in climate circles with blue-chip customers and celebrity investors, but a name resembling the Andean Pachamama and the unrelated Pachamama Alliance is confusable; no source states the origin.

outcome_analysis: Pachama rode the 2020 to 2022 corporate net-zero boom, raising $15M in April 2021 and a $55M Series B in May 2022 with Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon and Future Positive. Voluntary carbon markets then softened and offset quality was criticized; the company laid off about 20 people in summer 2025 and Carbon Direct announced its acquisition on November 10, 2025 for an undisclosed price, after roughly $88M raised.
notes: pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com (not fetched). The April 2021 TechCrunch article does not name the stage, so it is recorded as other. A $4.1M seed after YC (Contrary snippet) and a $9M Series B extension in Dec 2023 appear only on aggregators and are unverified, not recorded as rounds. Series B valuation reports ($200M, $275M) are from aggregators and conflict. Total raised about $88M per PitchBook via TechCrunch, $79M after Series B per one outlet. Origin of the name not found. Only competitor source found was dated Jan 2020 (Project Wren, Cloverly), too late to list as of founding.
